- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent history shows mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; apply a downward correction of 2–5% of the spike magnitude.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of a new trend; adjust downward by 1–3% for early forecast horizon.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model may lag; anticipate a rebound and adjust forecast upward by 1–2%.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and history shows volatility, model tends to be too smooth; add 0.5–1.5% volatility buffer to forecast.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to reflect new sentiment direction.
